purpose: Cefdinir is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as ear infections, sinus infections, strep throat, pneumonia, and some skin infections. It works only against bacteria, so it will not help with viral illnesses like the common cold or flu. Your doctor prescribed it because the bacteria causing your infection are likely to respond well to this medicine.
how_it_works: Cefdinir works by attacking the outer wall that surrounds bacteria, which bacteria need to survive. Without that protective wall, the bacteria fall apart and die. Think of it like poking holes in a balloon — once the shell is broken, the bacteria cannot hold together anymore.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are diarrhea, nausea, stomach upset, and headache. You may also notice that your stools turn a reddish color — this is harmless and happens because the medicine can react with iron in your gut or in certain foods like iron-fortified formula. This is not blood and is nothing to worry about.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you are allergic to penicillin or any other antibiotics, because some people who are allergic to penicillin may also react to cefdinir. Stop taking it and call your doctor right away if you develop a rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing, as these could be signs of a serious allergic reaction. Also let your doctor know if you have kidney problems, since your dose may need to be adjusted. Take all of your doses as directed, even if you feel better early, to make sure the infection is fully cleared.
typical_dosing: For most adults and teenagers, the usual dose is 300 mg twice a day or 600 mg once a day, taken for 5 to 10 days depending on the infection. For children, the dose is based on body weight and is usually given once or twice a day. You can take cefdinir with or without food, but avoid taking it at the same time as antacids containing aluminum or magnesium, or iron supplements, as these can reduce how well the medicine is absorbed — space them at least 2 hours apart.
